title: Psychological support for child refugees from Ukraine: Playful Arousal-, StressResilience-, Support-Training
summary: Children who have experienced traumatic events such as war, flight and destruction often show impairment in their psychosocial development and emotion regulation. Problems in emotion regulation, in turn, are linked to lower psychological resilience and numerous child and adolescent psychiatric disorders. To promote this resilience and reduce the risk of developing child and adolescent psychiatric disorders, the promotion of emotion regulation is an important approach. This is exactly where the START-Kids training programme comes in and aims to support children aged 6-12 years in their emotion regulation and resilience. In the present study, START-Kids will be slightly adapted and thus become PASST (Psychological Support for Refugee Children from Ukraine: Playful Arousal, Stress Resilience, Support Training) and carried out with children from Ukraine or other countries affected by war, flight and destruction. It is aimed at all affected children and no child and adolescent psychiatric diagnosis is required for participation. A clinical study will be conducted to investigate whether PASST helps to reduce the children's emotional problems. In addition, a healthy, age-matched control group without experiences of war or displacement will be included to investigate epigenetic and immunological changes associated with war, flight, and chronic stress. Children in the control group will not participate in the training program but will undergo the same pre-tests, post-tests, and follow-up assessments as the intervention group.

interventions.name: Intervention group: All children undergo pre-tests, post-tests, and follow-up tests after a longer interval, as well as group training, which takes place twice a week for one hour over a period of 8 weeks.

Control group: A healthy, age-matched comparison group without experiences of war or displacement undergoes the same pre-tests, post-tests, and follow-up tests after a longer interval as the intervention group, but does not participate in the group training.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
background of migration from Ukraine or other countries affected by war, flight and destruction
Exclusion criteria:
Testgroup: severe neurological and psychiatric conditions like psychosis, or substance use disorder of participant or primary caregiver 
Control group: Children will be excluded from participation in the control group if they or their parents have severe neurological or psychiatric disorders, such as psychosis or substance use disorders. Additionally, children must have no experiences of war, displacement, or other significant traumatic events.
